printed_header: I am pleased to submit my second annual report. The year 1984 has proved to be a very busy year, which, through both education and experience, has resulted in improved operations. As can be seen from the first page of this report, a hallmark of my administration has been to fully communicate with the townspeople. It is the responsibility of all public officials to report on a regular basis what they have done to better the town. This allows for feedback SO that voters have input between Town Meetings. Much has been studied and discussed about ways to improve town government. We are not faced with a crisis of management, rather we are faced with a crisis of communication. Changing the form of government may not enhance the exchange of information if there are still problems. We must solve the obvious problems, rather than trying to solve manufactured ones. There must be a free flowing communication without distrust on the part of any depart- ment. One solution is a monthly networking session of all Town department heads, with each, on a rotating basis, presenting a program on how it works. In order to serve the townspeople more conveniently, the three offices are now open on Thursday nights until 7 p.m. This coincides with the hours of Lunenburg banks, and will help those who work out of town to conduct town business. TREASURER
